item.title: Incoming GOP congressman backs halting all immigration to US, warns about Sharia law in Texas
item.description: Rep.-elect Jace Yarbrough says he favors stopping immigration altogether and repealing the 1965 Hart-Celler Act as he prepares to enter Congress.
item.content:encoded:
Rep.-elect Jace Yarbrough, a Republican from Texas, is set to enter Congress on Jan. 3 with an agenda to sharply restrict immigration and preserve what he describes as the "Christian heritage" of the United States, though he doubts the incoming Democratic majorities in both chambers will be willing to work with him.

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Yarbrough repeatedly denounced mass migration and said he'd be in favor of "stopping immigration altogether for a time because of how insane this has gotten."

He argued the U.S. is admitting far too many immigrants, including individuals he described as "avowedly anti-American" or connected to international terrorist groups.

He also said he'd support repealing the 1965 Hart-Celler Act, which abolished the national-origins quota system that favored immigrants from Northern and Western Europe while severely restricting immigration from Asia, Africa and other parts of the world.

'AMERICA FIRST' IMMIGRATION OVERHAUL BILL WOULD CODIFY TRUMP'S CAMPAIGN PROMISES ONCE AND FOR ALL

Asked whether he supported restoring national-origin quotas, Yarbrough instead advocated for a merit-based immigration system. Currently, most green cards are issued through family-based immigration, in which U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents sponsor eligible relatives. A much smaller share are issued based on employment qualifications and skills.

"You have to justify why it is that you are going to make our country stronger," Yarbrough said. "You have to prove that you want to be a part of this thing. You're going to forswear allegiance to your old country."

Yarbrough also expressed concerns about the spread of Sharia law, the Islamic religious legal system that he argued was "completely incompatible" with American values.

"We're not thoughtful about whether or not certain cultures are compatible with ours," he said. "My job as a member of Congress...is to fight for us and be unapologetic about the richness of our history."

When asked to provide examples of what he has previously described as the "Islamification of Texas," Yarbrough pointed to a lawsuit filed last year by the East Plano Islamic Center (EPIC), a North Texas mosque.

AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI

The EPIC mosque is located near Texas' 32nd Congressional District, which Yarbrough will be representing in Congress.

"That mosque sued a group of Christian street preachers for preaching the gospel on public sidewalks near the mosque. And that's an example of the kind of anti-American Sharia supremacist behavior, activity, and ideology that I'm talking about," Yarbrough said.

In Oct. 2025, the mosque sued Testimonies of God, a Texas-based Baptist ministry, alleging that its members used microphones and bullhorns to disrupt Friday prayer services in violation of the city's noise ordinance. Videos posted to the ministry's social media accounts show its members preaching near the mosque over a period of several months.

Plano police records show officers responded to a criminal trespass complaint at the mosque in May, though the log does not identify those involved or indicate whether a citation was issued. A judge dismissed EPIC's lawsuit in March under Texas' anti-SLAPP law, but the mosque appealed, and the case remains pending.

TEXAS AG PAXTON SUES EPIC CITY DEVELOPERS AFTER PROBE FINDS ALLEGED FRAUD, MISLEADING MUSLIM-ONLY MARKETING

Yarbrough's concerns about EPIC are similar to those of Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who repeatedly accused the mosque of attempting to establish a community governed by Sharia law.

But while Abbott lost his re-election bid to Democrat Gina Hinojosa, Yarbrough won his race with just over 51% of the vote, capturing a seat previously held by a Democrat as his party suffered sweeping losses nationwide.

Yarbrough's victory was aided by a 2025 redistricting effort that transformed the 32nd District from a Democratic stronghold into a Republican-leaning seat by adding several conservative rural counties east of Dallas.

Yarbrough, however, credited his win to his unwavering embrace of the "America First" agenda, arguing that Republicans should resist calls to moderate despite the party's poor performance in the midterms.

DEM WINS TRUMP-TARGETED TEXAS DISTRICT IN REBUKE OF REPUBLICAN REDISTRICTING SHAKEUP

He did acknowledge that some of his younger constituents were upset over the Iran war, with some of them expressing frustration that the conflict had contributed to higher gas prices.

"I didn't run away from any of the policy convictions of the America First movement," Yarbrough said. "Obviously that resonated with them because we were one of the few spots where Republicans were able to hold a seat and even gain a seat."

Yarbrough, a Stanford-educated attorney, served four years on active duty in the Air Force before transitioning to the reserve in 2015. He currently holds the rank of major and spends about five weeks a year serving at Space Systems Command at Cape Canaveral, Florida.

His decision to run for office was driven largely by his belief that the military and institutions where he studied and worked as a lawyer had become increasingly hostile to conservative values.

GOP WIPEOUT GOES FROM BAD TO WORSE AS DEMS QUIETLY SCORE ANOTHER MAJOR WIN WITH BIG RAMIFICATIONS

The consequences he faced after his refusal to take the COVID-19 vaccine on the "strong advice" of his doctor further pushed him toward a career in politics.

That decision earned him a formal reprimand from the Air Force, according to Yarbrough. He also said he resigned from Baker Botts, a prominent Texas law firm, the day before its vaccination policy took effect, which he said would have prevented him from entering the office without proof of vaccination.

Baker Botts did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Fox News Digital.

"The left just kept coming after me," Yarbrough said. "I finally decided, well, if they're not going to leave me alone, then upon evaluation, maybe it's my job to go and and fight to make them stop."

During a candidate forum in February, Yarbrough bluntly said, "I have no interest in representing Democrats," while talking about his vehement disagreement with COVID-19 vaccine mandates employers implemented during the height of the pandemic.

When asked about those comments, Yarbrough told Fox News Digital that he will represent the people of his district "whether they voted for me or not."

Yarbrough argued that many Texans who voted for Democrats were actually Republicans frustrated with their party, rather than supporters of progressive policies he considers extreme.

As he prepares to take office, Yarbrough said he was skeptical he'll find much common ground with his fellow Democrats in the House, who will steer the legislative priorities of the chamber for the next two years.

"It seems like they're going to be primarily interested in weaponizing, as they have several times in the past, whatever levers of power they've been given to try and go after...members of the First Family and the administration," he said.

Still, Yarbrough said he'd be ready to work with anyone who wants to prioritize the interests of American citizens.

item.title: Colorado football's struggles under Deion Sanders face a tough test against surging Houston
item.description: Houston's 7-2 Cougars face Deion Sanders' struggling 3-6 Colorado Buffaloes with college football playoff hopes potentially on the line Friday night.
item.content:encoded:
College Football gets an early start on some great action tonight as we have three football games, and two of the three games feature a top-25-ranked squad taking the field. The Friday slate doesn't always feature the higher-ranked teams, but we are treated tonight. I've picked out one of the games to place a wager on. Houston is taking on Colorado tonight, and we have a good chance to make some cash on the game.

The Houston Cougars are 7-2 for the season, and they've been competitive in every game they've played. Their two losses were to two of the other best teams in the Big 12, against Texas Tech and Utah. In the Texas Tech game, they fell 28-26 on the road. Quarterback Conner Weigman played well enough in the game; the team fell just short and couldn't come up with the winning drive. Against Utah, again on the road, the team lost 21-13. Houston was able to keep Utah from scoring in the first half and held a 13-7 lead going into the fourth quarter. They gave up two touchdowns and lost the game.

The Cougars are ranked 14th in the nation, and another loss would likely eliminate any and all hope of making the College Football Playoff. It may be hard for them to make the postseason bracket anyway. They haven't beaten a ton of impressive opponents. They beat Oklahoma State and Cincinnati in two of the past three weeks, but only the Cowboys were ranked. It does seem like the Cougars need to have a perfect game for them to beat some of the upper-echelon teams, but they shouldn't have any issues with tonight's opponent.

The Colorado Buffaloes were the talk of the college football world a few years ago when head coach Deion Sanders came into town. Sanders is a huge personality and brought in the top-ranked prospects into his program. His son was the quarterback, and the team had some talented pieces, but nothing that really was a full team. They were competitive enough, but in the two years since Travis Hunter and Shadeur Sanders have left, the Buffaloes have struggled significantly.

Sanders himself recently said he isn't cutting it. I have to agree. The team is 3-6 for the season, and they are 1-5 in Big 12 play. That doesn't mean that this team can't compete. They gave Utah quite a scare with a 27-24 contest, but again, couldn't get the play needed to close the deal. Colorado has lost four of their past five games, with the lone win over Kansas State University in overtime. I do want to give Colorado a bit of credit, at least; this wasn't a very easy schedule.

DAN DAKICH CALLS DEION SANDERS' COLORADO PROGRAM A 'TROJAN HORSE': 'THIS IS A S— SHOW'

Colorado has lost their six games by an average of 18.6 points per game. In fact, only one loss has been by seven points or fewer. Houston's wins have been by an average of 19.6 points per game. If we take out the anomaly of their 71-point win, they still are beating teams by 11 points. Colorado has done a solid job of playing better at home, but I don't see Houston taking it easy on them here. I'm taking Houston -9.5.

item.title: WWE's Brie Bella shares injury update after suffering broken scapula at SummerSlam
item.description: Brie Bella reveals her shattered scapula broke in five different spots at SummerSlam and shares her goal of resuming ring training in January.
item.content:encoded:
Brie Bella’s stunning return to WWE at the beginning of the year took a disastrous turn when she suffered a serious shoulder injury at SummerSlam in August.

Bella suffered a broken scapula during her tag team match with Paige against Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid. It marked the first time she suffered a significant injury in her WWE career and the overwhelming feelings of her Royal Rumble appearance and tag team victory with Paige at WrestleMania 42 simmered.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

The WWE Hall of Famer is now on the mend and gave an injury update to OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview ahead of her appearance at JP’s Brasserie and Sports Den in Las Vegas.

"Well, right now, I still have some breaks, unfortunately," she said. "We just got my CT scan back, but I'm hoping beginning of December, I'll have better news. So, I'm just keeping up with my physical therapy. Finally, I got to kind of go up the next level of physical therapy and that was really fun. It was really challenging so far this week. I was like, whoa, I haven't been this sore like since July.

"I'm hoping I can get back training in the ring in January. That is my goal. So, if the shoulder blade, if we see that everything is fused, then I can. If not, you know, I just, it's weird. It's been like a very interesting process because I shattered my shoulder blade. I broke it in like five different spots. So, it was like, it wasn't just one fracture, it was many. It's been interesting to see, see the progress. It's been a little too slow for me, but the doctor says I'm right on track."

Bella’s twin sister, Nikki, was also on the mend earlier this year after she suffered an ankle injury before WrestleMania 42. The injury led to Paige’s return.

But for fans who want to see the Bella Twin Power in action, it’s been a little disappointing.

"I don't know what 2026 was trying to tell the Bellas, but all it told us was broken bones," Brie Bella continued. "I'm hoping what it means is that when Nikki and I come back together in 2027, that the hype of us trying to come together to fight for the tag titles that it will just feel so powerful when we come in 2027.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I'm really looking forward to it and the minute the doctor clears me, I can't wait to start training again. When you're sitting and watching Raw, Smackdown as a fan, it's like you get all these ideas because I'm lucky I'm still part of it. So, it's like, I have a lot of fun ideas and I just really hope I can do them and I just can't wait for us both to be back in the ring."

Bella wouldn’t necessarily shed light on some of the ideas she had – at least when it came to storylines.

However, she had some thoughts about her ring gear.

"I mean like little things, so I'm not gonna tell you like storyline ideas like I want to pitch, but like fun stuff. I've been thinking about my gear – do I go back in the one I just wore my comeback? Do I kind of go off the vibe I had at SummerSlam? So, I've been kind of messing around with some different looks and, you know, or do I go major old school like Brie Mode? I don't know. It’s fun kind of getting creative and thinking of what to do."

Bella made her return to WWE at the Royal Rumble back in January. This year’s Royal Rumble, will take place at State Farm Stadium in Phoenix on Feb. 6. Maybe it will be the perfect time to come back once again.

item.title: Illegal immigrant trucker charged in crash that killed mom, 2 young sons heading to airport
item.description: A tablet with YouTube open was found in the semi-truck driven by Eldar Skander, who allegedly caused the fatal Kansas City crash at high speed.

Eldar Skander, 39, was charged with three counts of first-degree involuntary manslaughter in connection with a crash in Kansas City, Missouri, on Monday, according to a news release from the Jackson County Prosecutor's Office. A GoFundMe page identified the victims as 35-year-old Olga Sorbalo and her two children, 4-year-old Samir and 8-year-old Luis.

As traffic slowed to a stop, prosecutors said the Volvo semi-truck driven by Skander continued at a "high rate of speed" before striking a black Honda Odyssey, triggering a chain-reaction crash. item.title: Trump's spy chiefs put Republican leaders on the clock over 'huge priority' as power shift looms over Congress
item.description: Trump's intelligence chiefs set a Dec. 9 deadline for Congress to reauthorize FISA Section 702 before Democrats take control of Capitol Hill.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: President Donald Trump's top administration intelligence officials penned a letter to congressional leaders urging them to reauthorize the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA).

An administration official told Fox News Digital the intel measure is at top of mind for the White House to get passed in the still-Republican-controlled Congress before Democrats take a majority on Capitol Hill in January.

"This is going to be a huge priority and push by the administration, by the White House for the lame-duck Congress, because this really needs to get done," the administration source said. "Otherwise, we're kind of in trouble from a national security standpoint."

They stressed that the White House is "fully on board" with the push by the intelligence agencies' leaders asking Congress to reauthorize the law, including the controversial Section 702.

CONGRESS RETURNS TO BRUTAL LAME-DUCK STRETCH WITH SHUTDOWN DEADLINE, LEADERSHIP RACES: 'CLOSET IS FULL OF S—'

The letter, signed by Attorney General Todd Blanche, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and CIA Director John Ratcliffe, set a deadline for Dec. 9, 2026, less than a month before the new Congress will be sworn into office.

Clayton and Ratcliffe briefed the Gang of 8 — members of Congress who are legally apprised of classified national security matters and covert operations by the executive branch — earlier this week about the status of FISA.

TRUMP NOMINATES JAY CLAYTON, FORMER SEC CHAIRMAN, CURRENT US ATTORNEY, AS INTELLIGENCE DIRECTOR

"Any delays beyond this date will risk this critical authority lapsing, putting the lives of both Americans in the homeland and our troops stationed abroad at risk in the heightened threat environment briefed to the Gang of 8 earlier this week," the letter says.

It is addressed to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y.

SENATE TEMPORARILY EXTENDS NATION’S CONTROVERSIAL SPYING POWERS AFTER HOUSE FUMBLES

"As you know, Section 702 is the single most indispensable tool we have to keep our homeland and the American people safe," the letter says. "It enables our Intelligence Community to detect and disrupt terrorist plots, cyber intrusions, and weapons proliferation. No other authority can replace it."

FISA's Section 702 has a controversial history. Privacy activists and constitutional scholars have long argued that Section 702 is akin to warrantless surveillance. Under Section 702, intelligence agencies can clandestinely collect the communications of Americans if they are speaking to foreigners who are targets of investigations.

The Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) credits Section 702 for thwarting terrorist activities, including a mass casualty terror attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna, Austria, in 2024, and says that 63% of the articles in Trump's daily brief contained FISA Section 702 information reported by the National Security Agency in 2025.

JOHNSON FACES GOP REVOLT OVER WARRANTLESS SURVEILLANCE POWERS AHEAD OF KEY VOTE

The letter explains that the statutory authority of Section 702 has lapsed, and that collection of such materials will expire on March 16 if FISA is not reauthorized.

It goes on to say that the Dec. 9 congressional deadline to begin the renewal process will allow the intelligence agencies the necessary amount of time to complete the steps for continued Section 702 collection before the March expiration date.

LAWMAKERS SCRAMBLE AFTER TRUMP DERAILS BID TO REVIVE KEY COUNTERTERRORISM TOOL DAYS AFTER FBI THWARTS UFC PLOT

"To prevent a gap in critical intelligence and avoid putting our nation at risk, the government must start the 2027 renewal process by then," the letter states.

"If collection stops, we cannot simply turn 702 back on. The Administration looks forward to briefing Congress again in the coming days on the irreplaceable intelligence enabled by Section 702 and the dire risks to our nation if it is allowed to expire."

ODNI, the Department of Justice and the White House did not return Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

item.title: Could AI reduce shipping costs and grocery bills?
item.description: EAIGLE says its AI camera technology cuts truck check-ins from 10 minutes to under 30 seconds, potentially reducing fuel waste across supply chains.
item.content:encoded:
You walk into the grocery store and notice that some of your favorite products cost more than they used to. Then you order something online and discover the delivery fee has gone up, too. It's frustrating, especially when it feels like you're paying more for the same things. Now, here's something you probably haven't considered. Part of what you pay for everyday products can be tied to delivery trucks sitting in long lines outside warehouses. Those trucks can burn expensive diesel while drivers wait to check in. Meanwhile, transportation companies face higher operating expenses that can eventually find their way into retail prices.

According to the most recent update from the U.S. Energy Information Administration, the national average diesel price was $6.13 per gallon for the week of Nov. 9. That's still a significant expense for businesses moving products across the country. But what if artificial intelligence could help eliminate some of that waste?

A company called EAIGLE says its AI-powered camera technology can reduce truck check-ins at distribution centers from roughly 10 minutes to under 30 seconds. That could save trucking companies money. And if those savings spread across supply chains, they could potentially help reduce some of the cost pressures behind your grocery bill.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

TRUMP'S DIESEL IDEA COULD HAVE UNLEASHED A PROBLEM AMERICANS NEVER SAW COMING

You may never fill your car with diesel. However, chances are that much of the food in your kitchen traveled on a diesel-powered truck. Fresh produce often travels hundreds of miles before reaching your neighborhood supermarket. Many grocery products also move through distribution centers, where trucks unload incoming merchandise before stores receive their deliveries. Each trip costs money. When diesel prices rise, transportation companies often add fuel surcharges or increase shipping rates to cover the additional expense.

Those costs can eventually reach the companies selling products to you. In fact, a USDA-supported study examined how diesel prices and truck-driver availability affect food transportation. The researchers found that higher transportation costs generally increased food prices in the scenarios they studied. Potatoes were especially sensitive to changes in transportation expenses, partly because they're often shipped long distances from growing regions to major markets. So, while fuel prices are only one factor behind grocery inflation, they can have a real impact on what shoppers pay. And here's where AI could help.

Think about driving through an E-ZPass lane. Instead of stopping at a toll booth, technology handles the payment while traffic keeps moving. EAIGLE wants to bring a similar experience to warehouse gates. At many distribution centers, truck drivers still go through manual check-ins. Security personnel may need to review shipping documents and verify that the right truck has arrived for the right load.

During busy periods, those checks can create long lines. And when drivers leave their engines running, they're consuming fuel before they've even reached the loading dock. EAIGLE uses artificial intelligence and existing security cameras to automate much of that process. Its Automated Vehicle Access Control system, known as AVAC, identifies arriving vehicles and compares information against facility records. The company says its computer vision technology can capture more than 25 truck and trailer data points in under 30 seconds. That includes license plate numbers and other identifying details that help determine whether a vehicle should enter the property.

When the information matches, an automated gate can allow the driver to proceed. If something looks suspicious, the system can flag the vehicle for additional review. EAIGLE says this reduces a process that typically takes around 10 minutes to less than 30 seconds. Now, saving a few minutes might not sound like much. But consider a major distribution center processing hundreds of trucks every day. Reducing repeated delays could help companies use less fuel and avoid unnecessary operating expenses.

Here's the question I think is worth asking. If artificial intelligence helps companies spend less money moving products, could some of those savings reach shoppers? Potentially, yes. But there's an important catch. Transportation costs are built into the economics of getting products onto store shelves. If a grocery chain can reduce those expenses, it may have more room to hold prices steady when other costs increase. The same idea applies to online shopping. Shipping companies often include fuel surcharges in their rates, which can affect what retailers charge for delivery.

Reducing wasted fuel could help offset some of that expense. However, there's currently no evidence that EAIGLE's technology has directly lowered grocery prices or delivery fees for shoppers. Retailers could use the savings to offset other expenses or improve their profits. And because freight-yard check-ins account for only a small part of overall transportation costs, any savings would need to add up across many facilities to have a noticeable impact on what families pay. Still, with shipping expenses affecting so many products, it's an area worth watching.

Price is one concern. But what about finding the products you actually want? We've all gone shopping for something specific, only to discover that the store is out of stock. And there's nothing particularly satisfying about tracking an online order that seems stuck somewhere between a warehouse and your front door. Distribution delays can contribute to those frustrations.

If trucks spend less time waiting at warehouse gates, facilities may be able to process incoming shipments more efficiently. That could help retailers keep merchandise moving through their networks. For example, a grocery distribution center that receives deliveries more smoothly may have an easier time keeping scheduled shipments moving toward individual stores.

However, faster check-ins alone won't guarantee fuller shelves or earlier deliveries. Trucks can still encounter traffic delays, and warehouses may face shortages or loading dock congestion. The potential benefit comes when companies reduce delays throughout the entire shipping process.

DELIVERY DRONES COULD BE WAITING BEFORE YOU EVEN ORDER

EAIGLE estimates that a facility using its technology could save approximately $726,000 annually through improvements in gate operations and other efficiencies. The company also estimates that a facility processing around 200 trucks daily could eliminate approximately 110,000 pounds of carbon dioxide emissions each year by reducing unnecessary idling. That's roughly 55 U.S. tons of carbon dioxide. These are company-provided estimates, and actual results would depend on the facility and its operations.

There's another expense that can affect the supply chain. Cargo theft. Criminals sometimes pose as legitimate transportation companies to collect shipments they have no authority to take. According to a June 2026 FBI warning, estimated cargo theft losses across the United States and Canada reached nearly $725 million in 2025. That's an enormous amount of stolen merchandise.

EAIGLE says its system can help identify suspicious pickups by comparing truck information with shipping records. If a vehicle arrives with incorrect identification or paperwork, the software can flag the problem. The company claims its technology can reduce theft and fraud exposure by more than 50%. Preventing stolen shipments could help retailers avoid some expensive losses. It may also reduce disruptions when merchandise disappears before reaching its destination.

According to EAIGLE, its technology is already being used in major North American distribution facilities, including operations associated with Walmart. Meanwhile, Loblaw Companies Limited, one of Canada's largest grocery and pharmacy retailers, is expanding its relationship with EAIGLE. In a September 2026 announcement, Loblaw confirmed plans to expand the company's AI-powered gate technology across multiple distribution centers. The retailer says early results showed improvements in processing times and data accuracy. The technology also helped improve the experience for truck drivers arriving at its facilities.

Wael Yehia, Loblaw's vice president of national transportation, explained that the company is looking for practical ways to move products more efficiently through its distribution network. That's worth paying attention to because grocery retailers handle enormous volumes of merchandise. Improvements at busy distribution centers could help make those operations more reliable.

Here's why I think this technology is worth following, even if you never visit a freight yard. Every product that reaches your home has a transportation story behind it. Fuel costs affect that journey, and inefficiencies can add expenses long before a retailer puts a price tag on an item. AI systems like EAIGLE's could help transportation companies reduce some of those costs. Faster gate operations may also help retailers keep deliveries on schedule, which could improve product availability. For shoppers, the biggest potential benefit is relief from rising prices. If companies can operate more efficiently, they may be better positioned to absorb transportation costs instead of passing every increase along.

I think one of the most interesting things about AI right now is where it's starting to show up. We hear so much about robots taking over jobs in warehouses and trucks that drive themselves. But here's an example of AI tackling something as simple as a long line of trucks waiting to enter a warehouse. And when you start connecting those delays to fuel expenses and the cost of shipping everyday products, you can see why this technology has potential. What I like about EAIGLE's approach is that companies can use cameras they may already have installed. They don't necessarily need a fleet of new trucks or expensive changes to their facilities to start improving operations. For now, I see this as a promising example of AI addressing a real supply chain problem. The next step is proving that the improvements go beyond the warehouse gate. And if those savings eventually help keep grocery prices or delivery fees from climbing even higher, that's something we can all appreciate.

If AI helps Walmart and other major retailers save hundreds of thousands of dollars moving merchandise, should they pass those savings on to shoppers? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

item.title: Americans warned to avoid crowds in major city amid unprecedented police operation
item.description: Americans are warned by the U.S. Embassy in Dublin about road closures, protests and transport disruptions tied to a massive European leaders summit.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. officials are warning Americans in Dublin to stay alert Friday amid a major security operation surrounding a gathering of European leaders — and the event has already brought protests to the Irish capital.

The warning was issued by the U.S. Embassy in Dublin this week ahead of two European leaders' summits scheduled for Thursday and Friday.

While the embassy warned the heaviest disruptions were expected Thursday, security measures were scheduled to remain in place through Friday, with road closures and transportation disruptions affecting central Dublin.

US WARNS AMERICANS TO AVOID FAMED TOURIST SQUARE AFTER GUNMAN KILLS 6, INJURES 15

The embassy said some 50 European leaders were expected to attend the ninth European Political Community summit and an informal European Council meeting to discuss strategic priorities under Ireland's EU presidency.

Irish police, known as An Garda Síochána, launched what the embassy described as the largest security and policing operation in the country's history.

Pictures what appear to be hundreds of police on guard in Dublin as protesters flooded streets, many of them carrying Palestinian flags.

‘DO NOT PHYSICALLY RESIST’: US ISSUES CHILLING ROBBERY WARNING FOR AMERICANS OVERSEAS

"Expect protests, security cordons and transport disruptions across central Dublin starting as early as Nov. 10, 2026," the embassy warned in its statement.

The alert covered several prominent locations in central Dublin, including the Convention Centre Dublin.

Dublin Castle and the National Gallery of Ireland — two popular tourist attractions — were also covered in the alert.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The Irvine Police Department released surveillance videos on social media showing people taking part in the "Door Kick Challenge," which involves kicking someone's front door as hard as possible, recording it and running away before anyone answers.

"This isn't a prank. It's vandalism, and it can end badly," the department said.

item.content:encoded:
Ethan Page made his WWE main roster debut on the "Monday Night Raw" after WrestleMania 42 and set out on a near-six-month journey to chase the Intercontinental Championship.

It wasn’t an easy task for "All Ego." He initially lost at his first opportunity against Penta at Saturday Night’s Main Event back in May. However, his fortunes changed drastically earlier this month.

"It feels great. I mean, I wish you could know so that I wouldn't have to describe it, but I don't know if that's possible," he told OutKick Dropkick. "I don't know, I feel, legendary."

The WWE Intercontinental Championship is an illustrious title. Legendary wrestlers like Chris Jericho, Triple H, Razor Ramon, The Rock, Shawn Michaels, Bret Hart, Randy Savage and others have held the title at least once.

Raising the prestige of an already legendary championship is no easy task. OutKick Dropkick asked the Canadian superstar how he was going to go about accomplishing that.

"Well, I'm not going to change anything about it," he said. "And I think that, in itself, adds to the prestige because I'm not willing to bend the knee to nostalgia. I don't need a previous anything to prop me up. I will be adding everything to the championship. Whatever I do with the Intercontinental Championship will be solely by my contributions. Nothing to do with the physical championship or its history at all. With me, only addition. It will only grow, it will only become more impactful, it will only become more important. And when in, this very specific championship, 20 years from now, 30 years from now, this will be the thing that all the wrestlers, that never got rid of their fandom, like half the guys in the locker room right now, that wish they were intercontinental champions, so they could bring back the white strap or the oval or whatever peak fandom of their childhood that they're trying to replicate or duplicate or live vicariously through, makes me sick to my stomach what's happened in professional wrestling is half cosplay now, me,

"I'm gonna make what I hold legendary, what I won legendary. I was actually upset they took Chad's side plates off. I wish they just left them on. It's part of history. It's the man that I beat, that's the prize that I won, and they've already altered the championship that I won, and it kind of breaks my heart a little bit. I'm gonna make sure that in 20 years from now, whatever dummy that follows in the footsteps of all the wrestlers today, is begging their boss, who will probably be me anyways, to bring back this design, so that they could live vicariously through me like all the loser wrestlers try and live vicariously through their favorites."

item.title: The mistake newly-elected Dems admit they can't afford to make with Trump after sweeping 2026 wins
item.description: Newly elected Democrats at a Denver conference urged their party to work with Donald Trump on costs and policy rather than focus solely on investigations.
item.content:encoded:
DENVER — Congressional Democrats are heading into the next two years with a choice: focus on investigating President Donald Trump and his administration or look for ways to work with him to deliver results for Americans.

The party, after sweeping pickups in last week's midterms, right away warned Trump and Republicans to "lawyer up" and in the following days began outlining investigations into the administration, including its handling of immigration enforcement, the president’s business interests and the Justice Department's actions.

But newly elected Democrats and strategists at the "What’s Next" conference in Denver told Fox News Digital that their party should seek opportunities to work with Trump.

The new guard argues that voters who elected them into office want to see results over partisan fights.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

Hosted by Majority Democrats, the conference brought Democratic leaders, strategists and rising figures together to discuss the party’s direction after the midterms. Organizers billed it as an independent conversation about what Democrats should do next.

Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand cautioned his party against making investigations and impeachments the focus of its new political momentum, particularly when the underlying issues have already been reported.

Asked what he did not want Democrats to do as they take office, Sand said he did not want to see them "throwing bombs" at Republicans. Voters, he said, need public servants focused on improving their lives.

"There are people who are really struggling right now, whose lives have been ruined by high gas prices, by all kinds of policy choices, and they need results," Sand told Fox News Digital. "They need public servants who are actually trying to serve the public."

BERNIE SANDERS WARNS DEMOCRATS NOT TO SPEND ALL THEIR TIME INVESTIGATING TRUMP

Sand said he questioned the value of investigating matters already covered by the media instead of pursuing work that could help ordinary people. Asked if that meant working with the Trump administration, he said yes.

"He’s there, he was put there two years ago. He’s gonna be there another two years," Sand said. "You don’t get to pick and choose who you work with. The people do."

Sen.-elect James Talarico, D-Texas, called on Democrats to focus on what they can accomplish now, even as they push for longer-term reforms.

"Some of these reforms may not pass until 2029, but the American people cannot wait two years for change," Talarico said. "We must work with President Trump."

He urged Democrats to make the Republican president's final two years in office "the most productive of any presidency in American history."

Talarico, who became the first Democrat in nearly four decades to win a statewide election in Texas, also warned against getting "bogged down in the same petty fights."

"The American people are demanding change, and in this election, they chose our party to deliver it," Talarico said.

Democratic strategist Lis Smith offered a related caution, saying the election was "largely a referendum on Donald Trump and less a validation of Democrats and their policies."

Smith, a senior advisor for Majority Democrats, said the party still needs to earn voters’ trust and should focus on costs and corruption rather than treating their wins as a mandate for policies they did not campaign on. She also said that Democrats didn't sweep because of their winning message, but rather because fed-up voters cast their ballots as a rebuke of Trump and his policies.

"We should not read into these election results as a mandate for far left policies advocated only by a handful of candidates," Smith emphasized.

VOTERS PUNISHED THE GOP OVER COSTS; NOW, DEMOCRATS FACE THE AFFORDABILITY TEST

And it appears many voters agree.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll published this month indicated that nearly three-quarters of Americans wanted Democratic leaders in Congress to make a concerted effort to work with the president.

item.title: Alito warns against congressional Supreme Court meddling, says some lower court judges 'have gone far astray'

"Congress can turn off the lights at the Supreme Court and stop everything from happening if they want to defund their activities. And there are many, many, many other things that they can do, or at least try to do," Alito said during remarks at the Federalist Society's Antonin Scalia Memorial Dinner, the outlet reported.

"So, it is important to preserve the independence of the judiciary," he reportedly said. "If that is eliminated, then the Constitution as adopted in 1789 will no longer be the same."

ALITO REITERATES HE'S NOT RETIRING, IS COMMITTED THROUGH END OF CURRENT SUPREME COURT TERM

While Congress could target the Supreme Court's funding, the U.S. Constitution explicitly protects the pay of high court justices.

"The judicial Power of the United States, shall be vested in one supreme Court, and in such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish. The Judges, both of the supreme and inferior Courts, shall hold their Offices during good Behaviour, and shall, at stated Times, receive for their Services, a Compensation, which shall not be diminished during their Continuance in Office," Article III, Section 1 of the Constitution reads.

TRUMP'S SUPREME COURT MAJORITY FACES LOOMING THREAT AFTER DEM SENATE TAKEOVER: 'STUCK'

Alito indicated that lower-level judges have at times handed down "unjustified" orders obstructing the policies of presidents during recent years, The Hill reported.

"They are dedicated, and they are skillful, but they're not perfect, and they make mistakes," he said, according to the report. "And in some instances, I think they have gone far astray in abuse of their powers."

item.title: NASCAR star delivers a brutal reality check after fans turned off the championship race
item.description: Denny Hamlin challenged NASCAR to become relevant again in the sports landscape after championship race viewership dropped nearly 11% from last year.
item.content:encoded:
The NASCAR season is officially over, which means it's time to dust off the 'ol mirror and do some good, hard looking in it.

A little self-reflection never hurt anyone. Every league should do it, frankly. There are always things to improve upon after a season. No matter if it went good, bad or indifferent, every league can do better.

NASCAR is no different. In fact, I'd argue this is maybe the most consequential offseason the sport has faced in some time.

NASCAR'S NEW VILLAIN PICKS ANOTHER VICTIM AND FANS WANT HIM PARKED, DRIVER FLIES WITH TRUMP & RATINGS REBOUND?

The big question? How do they get folks watching — and following — the series again? That's not me talking, by the way. That comes straight from the mouth of Denny Hamlin, NASCAR's oldest and biggest star.

"We have got to find a way to grow this thing and make it more relevant in the sports landscape, because it's just falling behind others in my opinion," Hamlin said on his Actions Detrimental podcast on the heels of Sunday's anticlimactic championship race.

"Our sport is different. It's not this one-v-one and it's either you or me, you know, and so we have to just embrace that this is what we wanted. We wanted a bigger sample size for the champion for it to feel right. I think it feels right. And so, it's going to always feel a little different, but it's our jobs as a sport to make it relevant in sports.

"And that's that's what I challenge more than anything ... we have got to make our sport relevant again when it comes to the general sports landscape."

HAS NASCAR LOST THE SOUTH? EX-DRIVER UNLOADS AFTER SEEING "100,000 EMPTY SEATS"

Amen, Denny! Say it louder for the people in the back. Shout it. I've been saying NASCAR has a relevancy problem all season long, and the latest batch of TV ratings don't do it any favors.

Sunday's race at Homestead got a 1.37 rating and averaged 2.471 million viewers, which was a nearly 11% drop from last year's title race at Phoenix. I'm not going to sit here and call it the least watched championship race ever, because, frankly, I don't feel like getting a call from NASCAR today.

It's a Friday. I've got things to do. I don't feel like getting into a long debate about how Nielsen measures things. Trying to compare things to the old days doesn't work, so I'm not going to do it. I know it's more complicated today.

I do not care.

The number is the number. The number was not great, again. Overall on the season, viewership was down 2%.

Here's the question we need to first answer ...

Who does this fall on? Seriously. Who's fault is it? Remember, this is mirror-looking time, folks! Start looking!

The fans? The car? The racing? The 14 different channels? All of the above?

It's a fair question, because there is an argument to be made that the fans didn't hold up their end of the bargain.

HOW KYLE LARSON TURNED A WRITE-OFF SEASON INTO HIS THIRD NASCAR CHAMPIONSHIP IN MIAMI

Don't forget, all we talked about last offseason was how horrible the old playoff format was. You all hated it because you said it was too gimmicky. Everyone freaked out because Joey Logano won a championship two years ago, so NASCAR decided to blow it all up and start over.

I'm not saying going back to the old Chase format was the wrong call, but the fans begged for it and then didn't show up to watch a championship race on Sunday that was already decided.

Obviously, fans will point to the car, which has been another contentious topic all season. Fans do not like the Next Gen car. Drivers don't, either, but they can't say it as loudly as the fans can.

I get hundreds of emails every week about NASCAR. Hundreds. Do you know the most common complaint I hear?

"The car stinks. It's too slow, it doesn't look like a stock car, and it doesn't race well."

The car and Leigh Diffey — two things fans don't love. Sorry, Leigh.

Unfortunately, the car is the car, and the format is the format. As Denny said, neither are going away. NASCAR, and the fans, are stuck with both right now. It's on NASCAR to make the series relevant again.

"It ain't the car or the format," Hamlin continued. "It's much bigger than that. It's way bigger than that."

It's the promotion. That's the problem, Hamlin added. Outside of the Daytona 500, NASCAR simply isn't doing enough to promote the sport.

He might be right.

"I know we tried the whole midweek night races thing, but there was no promotion behind that at all," Hamlin continued. "I feel like the viewership number now is at a point where there I just ... what do you have to lose in that sense? Why can't we own Thursday night in the summer? You know when, when it's just baseball?

"Like own a night during the summer ... I'd love to see us try to own a night of the week during the summer when there's not much other sports on."

Ding, ding, ding! There it is! Does Denny read Monday Morning Pit-Stop? He has to. I've been barking up that tree for years now. Years. Ever since COVID.

Own the spring. Own the summer. STOP going up against football in the fall. Those are easy fixes you can implement right away. Next season. I know it would be a little difficult because the schedule is already out, but who cares? Tear it up and start over.

Give us midweek races in June and July. Give us a full summer of NASCAR. Shorten the season and have it end on Labor Day weekend. Promote the crap out of it. Market it like there is no tomorrow.

The car ain't going anywhere, folks. NASCAR is in too deep. They'll keep trying to improve it, but I'd imagine there's only so many more screws that tighten on it at this point.

The format isn't changing, either. It just did! They can't possibly mess with it again, can they? Not this soon.

The two things NASCAR can control? The schedule and the promotion.

Denny Hamlin said the quiet part out loud: NASCAR has a major relevancy problem right now.

They have three months to fix it.

item.title: Hispanic voters are natural conservatives. Reagan knew. GOP needs to prove it again
item.description: Donald Trump's border security record became a 2026 liability after indiscriminate deportation enforcement alienated hispanic voters, a Republican congressman argues.
item.content:encoded:
President Ronald Reagan famously told Hispanic adviser Lionel Sosa that Latinos were Republicans who "just don’t know it yet." President Donald Trump’s breakthrough in 2024 demonstrated that potential. Hispanic voters registered among the largest shifts toward Republicans — then swung sharply against us in 2026, reversing much of that progress.

Hispanics did not abandon faith, family and freedom. Our party gave too many reasons to question whether we were governing by those principles.

I understand the work of rebuilding trust. In 2020, I defeated a Democratic incumbent and flipped a congressional district from blue to red. As a career firefighter, fire chief and mayor, I learned that confidence comes from service and results.

MAMDANI MESSAGE TO RESIDENTS ON HOW TO DEAL WITH ICE RESULTS IN VIRAL INTERNET BACKLASH: 'TREASON'

Trump delivered extraordinary results securing the border. His administration restored consequences for illegal entry and backed our Border Patrol agents. Federal officials reported historically low crossings and zero Border Patrol releases throughout fiscal year 2026. Republicans had a signature accomplishment to showcase.

MULLIN VOWS ‘ZERO CHANGE’ ON IMMIGRATION AFTER REPUBLICANS SUFFER CRUSHING MIDTERM LOSSES

Yet indiscriminate immigration enforcement undermined public support for it. Enforcement against longtime, peaceful residents shifted attention from dangerous criminals to frightened families. Democrats gained an opening we should never have given them, and the president’s signature accomplishment was turned into a liability at the ballot box.

I warned about this before the election. Americans wanted violent criminals deported, gangs dismantled and neighborhoods protected. They did not vote to deport abuelas who spent decades raising families and contributing to their communities.

We have the solutions: enforce lawful removal orders with due process. Exercise judgment and examine cases individually, considering criminal history, family ties, years here and economic contributions. Congress should develop legal options for longtime, peaceful contributors, including DREAMers, while preserving ironclad border security.

WHITE HOUSE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER TRUMP ANGERS BASE BY FLOATING ILLEGAL ALIEN DEAL WITH DEMS

We also had an economic record to run on. Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill expanded the child tax credit, created Trump Accounts, delivered "no tax on tips" relief for eligible workers and provided an additional senior deduction that helps more retirees avoid federal income taxes on Social Security. These achievements deserved attention and directly benefited Hispanic families.

Build on them: unleash American innovation, cut unnecessary regulations, expand domestic energy and help entrepreneurs grow.

Abroad, we must finish the job in Iran, ensuring the regime can never threaten the United States and our allies with nuclear weapons. America must defend and protect democracy, especially in our own Western Hemisphere.

LATINO VOTERS SWING BACK TO DEMOCRATS AHEAD OF MIDTERM ELECTIONS: POLL

In Venezuela, Trump’s historic capture of dictator Nicolás Maduro opened the door to freedom. Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s three-phase plan — stabilization, recovery and transition — must lead to a genuine democratic transition, culminating in free and fair elections as quickly as possible. And in Cuba, we must fulfill Trump’s promise to bring freedom to the Cuban people.

Before 2028, return to our neighborhoods, listen and deliver.

Faith, family, freedom. Protect the border achievement. Restore judgment in enforcement. Deliver prosperity. Stand for democracy and freedom in our hemisphere. Do the hard work, and Republicans can earn back Hispanic voters’ confidence, creating a lasting, unbreakable majority-making coalition for years to come.

item.title: Disney alum David Henrie draws firm line on Hollywood intimate scenes that 'violate' his marriage
item.description: Actor David Henrie revealed on "The Unplanned Podcast" that he refuses nudity, sex scenes and kissing roles out of respect for his marriage.
item.content:encoded:
Actor David Henrie drew a firm line regarding his Hollywood career, saying he refuses to take on roles involving nudity, sex scenes or kissing out of respect for his marriage.

"For me, I draw the line if it’s anything that would actually violate our relationship as a married couple," Henrie told Matt and Abby Howard’s "The Unplanned Podcast" on Tuesday.

Appearing alongside his wife, Maria Cahill, the "Wizards of Waverly Place" alum, 37, outlined his acting boundaries, specifically citing "nudity" before Cahill chimed in with a laugh.

ANGEL STUDIOS DRAWS LINE IN SAND WITH HOLLYWOOD, BANS SEX SCENES, PROFANITY IN BOLD NEW PLEDGE

"He's not kissing anybody," she said.

Cahill, who married Henrie in 2017, suggested her husband is more concerned about such scenes than she is, emphasizing the trust she has in him.

"I feel like he cares more than I care," she said.

"I so trust him, I literally don’t care. He's like, 'I will not kiss [someone else],'" she added.

Henrie explained that his general rule is to accept roles as long as they do not conflict with his conscience or personal values, drawing a distinction between portraying fictional wrongdoing and performing intimate scenes.

"If I have to kill someone, like, I’m not really killing someone, you know? You can fake that," he explained.

MICHAEL DOUGLAS GETS EXPLICIT ABOUT HOW HE FILMED SEX SCENES BEFORE INTIMACY COORDINATORS

"[With intimate scenes] you’re not faking that ... You’re really doing that thing ... You’re in bed making out ..." he added later. "I don’t care how much you’re thinking of bees and birds, or whatever you’re doing to distract yourself. You’re really doing that."

Henrie said performing such scenes would "feel weird," retierating, "I'm not going to do it."

The conversation also turned to Henrie's time playing Justin Russo on Disney Channel's "Wizards of Waverly Place," when he filmed a kissing scene with his character's love interest years before marrying Cahill.

The couple recalled how their four children reacted after watching the episode, prompting questions about why he was showing affection to someone other than their mother.

"They were like, ‘You have another wife?’ Like, they were so upset," Cahill laughed.

"They’ll randomly bring it up, like, ‘Papa kissed another woman,’" Henrie added. "And they’ll go up to her and be like, ‘Papa has a girlfriend.’ It’s so funny."

'ANT-MAN' STAR EVANGELINE LILLY SAYS SHE LEFT HOLLYWOOD BECAUSE SHE 'ALWAYS HATED BEING FAMOUS'

Henrie, a devout Catholic, has been open about his faith and the repercussions of his commitment to Christ while acting in Hollywood.

During an appearance on the "Bryce Crawford Podcast" earlier this year, Henrie was asked what his faith cost him regarding his career.

"It was rough, lost my agents," he said.

"I walked away from a lot. I turned down a lot of roles. I was like I'm just not going to do something that I think will disrespect my belief now or disrespect our Lord. I'm just not going to do it. I'm not going to go near it. And it cost me a lot. It cost a lot. I lost a lot of money. Friends, a girlfriend at the time. I kind of was stripped of everyone, everyone that I would call a friend."

Henrie added that he made new friends that challenged him, which eventually led to him meeting his wife.

Fox News Digital's Hanna Panreck contributed to this report.
